claim.quote: Determination of the Number of Light Neutrino Species

date.note: INSPIRE preprint_date (October 1989) shared by all four papers.

key_value.note: Final LEP+SLD combined value from the 2006 precision-electroweak combination (see result:lep-electroweak-precision-2006), reused here as the best available number for the '3 neutrino species' conclusion. The individual October 1989 papers gave, with much larger errors: ALEPH 3.27+/-0.30, L3 3.42+/-0.48, DELPHI 2.4+/-0.4(stat)+/-0.5(syst), OPAL 3.1+/-0.4.
key_value.quote: The number of light neutrino species is determined to be 2.9840+/-0.0082.

key_value_text.quote: Nv=3.27+/-0.30" (ALEPH); "3.42+/-0.48 number of neutrino flavors" (L3); "N nu =2.4+/-0.4 (stat.) +/-0.5 (syst.)" (DELPHI); "3.1 +/- 0.4 neutrino generations" (OPAL)
key_value_text.value: Four independent 1989 measurements (ALEPH, L3, DELPHI, OPAL) each found a number of light neutrino species consistent with exactly 3; the number was later refined to 2.9840+/-0.0082 using the full LEP+SLD dataset.

name: Determination of the Number of Light Neutrino Species
notes: This entity records the historic 1989 determination that Nu=3; the final precision value (2.9840+/-0.0082) is reused here from the 2006 combination paper (also recorded separately as result:lep-electroweak-precision-2006) because no more precise 1989-dated combined figure was found in this session's sources. date/date_kind reflect the 1989 papers; key_value reflects the best available number.

ALEPH's own paper title is used as claim.quote because it states the result plainly ('Determination of the Number of Light Neutrino Species'); L3, DELPHI and OPAL used different titles for the same Z-lineshape analysis (see key_value_text).

summary.plain: Within weeks of LEP switching on, its four detectors measured how 'fat' the Z boson's resonance peak is - and found it was exactly the width expected for three, and only three, light neutrino types.
summary.technical: In October 1989 ALEPH, DELPHI, L3 and OPAL each independently measured the invisible partial width of the Z resonance and reported a number of light neutrino species (Nu) consistent with 3: ALEPH Nu=3.27+/-0.30, L3 Nu=3.42+/-0.48, DELPHI Nu=2.4+/-0.4(stat)+/-0.5(syst), OPAL Nu=3.1+/-0.4, each in Phys. Lett. B231 (1989) 509-547. The combined final LEP+SLD precision value, Nu=2.9840+/-0.0082, was published later in Phys. Rept. 427 (2006) 257.

title: Determination of the Number of Light Neutrino Species
why_it_matters: Ruled out a fourth generation of ordinary matter with a light neutrino, fixing the number of families of fundamental fermions at three and shaping every particle-physics model since.
